newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-DEFIANT DE SILVA ENDS TEST RUN DROUGHT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DEFIANT DE SILVA ENDS TEST RUN DROUGHT.

text.p: Aravinda de Silva ended his test cricket run drought with a timely 79 not out to lead a Sri Lanka fightback against Pakistan on the fourth day of the first test on Tuesday.
De Silva, who has been batting superbly in limited overs internationals, resisted for 262 minutes to hit his first half-century in 15 test innings.
His last test effort of over 50 was also against Pakistan, when he made 105 at Faisalabad in September 1995.

Thanks to de Silva and captain Arjuna Ranatunga, who struck 58 as they shared a third wicket partnership of 129, Sri Lanka ended the penultimate day on 206 for three in their second innings - a lead of 158.
De Silva's superb and chanceless innings against some high-class spin bowling by Saqlain Mushtaq and Mushtaq Ahmed was the feature of the day.
After a cautious start, de Silva displayed his full range of strokes, taking 14 runs off one over from paceman Mohammed Zahid which included a superbly hooked six over mid-wicket.
De Silva completed his 14th test half-century with a pull off Mushtaq for his sixth four. It took him 98 balls in 124 minutes, and he hit seven fours and one six altogether.
With Ranatunga playing the supporting role, the pair carried Sri Lanka to safety after Saqlain had sent back both openers when the overall lead was only five runs.

Ranatunga was out shortly before close, playing a tired stoke and offering Rameez Raja a simple catch at backward square leg. His 25th test half-century, which came in 206 minutes, comprised five fours.
Sri Lanka opened with Marvan Atapattu and Russell Arnold because regular opener Sanath Jayasuriya has the flu.
Both players fell to catches by Nazir on either side of the wicket off Saqlain. Arnold made 15 before mis-reading a slower ball and Atapattu, tied down by some accurate bowling, lost patience.
Pakistan, resuming in the morning at 370 for nine, added only eight runs before the last wicket stand of 29 was broken when Arnold ran out Saqlain with a direct hit from the covers.
Saqlain made 58 in a stay of 301 minutes, hitting five fours.
Pakistan are playing just two tests on their short tour.
